item.title: Paraguay’s president, Santiago Peña, resigns and is impeached within minutes
item.description:
Brought down by the collapse of Ueno, a digital bank that claimed more than 60% of the country’s adults as customers, the head of state announced his departure on Thursday. Deputies voted to impeach him straight afterwards.

On Thursday 5 November, in a video posted on X, Paraguay’s president, Santiago Peña, announced his resignation in the name of "social peace" and institutional stability, minutes before the lower house voted by 78 to 0 to impeach him and send him for trial in the Senate. His fall stems from the collapse of Ueno, a digital bank seized by the central bank on 3 November after poorly documented loans to firms linked to its owners came to light, and which held some $800m in public deposits; Horacio Cartes, leader of the Colorado Party, had already abandoned him. Congress is due to rule on the resignation on Friday, which would allow the vice-president, Pedro Alliana, to be sworn in without awaiting a trial, while the opposition wants him removed from office, which would strip Mr Peña of the life seat in the Senate, with its legal immunity, reserved for former presidents.
